_meta.indication: TECVAYLI is indicated for the treatment of adult patients with relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma who have received at least four prior lines of therapy, including a proteasome inhibitor, an immunomodulatory agent and an anti-CD38 monoclonal antibody.

pivotal_trials.design: Ongoing, first-in-human, single-arm, multicenter, multicohort trial evaluating teclistamab monotherapy
pivotal_trials.population: Adult patients with relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma; efficacy population all triple-class exposed with a median of 5 prior lines of therapy (78% had at least 4 prior lines), 76% triple-class refractory
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Overall response rate (ORR) assessed by an Independent Review Committee (IRC)
pivotal_trials.result: ORR 61.8% (95% CI: 52.1, 70.9); median DOR not reached; estimated DOR rate 90.6% at 6 months and 66.5% at 9 months

key_safety: Key safety concerns are cytokine release syndrome (CRS, 72%) and neurologic toxicity (57%), including ICANS (6%). Most common adverse reactions (>=20%) are pyrexia, cytokine release syndrome, musculoskeletal pain, injection site reaction, fatigue, upper respiratory tract infection, nausea, headache, pneumonia, and diarrhea.
target_moa: Teclistamab is a bispecific BCMA-directed and CD3-directed antibody that binds BCMA on multiple myeloma cells and CD3 on T-cells, promoting T-cell dependent elimination of BCMA-expressing cells.

boxed_warning.content: Boxed warning for Cytokine Release Syndrome (including life-threatening or fatal reactions) and Neurologic Toxicity including ICANS.

rems.type: TECVAYLI is available only through a restricted program under a REMS with elements to assure safe use (ETASU) to mitigate the risks of CRS and neurologic toxicity, including ICANS.

advisory_committee.vote: An Advisory Committee Meeting was not held, and no external consultations were requested.

description.text: Added a reduced biweekly dosing regimen (1.5 mg/kg every two weeks) for patients maintaining complete response or better for at least 6 months

citations.quote: This Prior Approval sBLA provides for updates to the Tecvayli (teclistamab-cqvy) US Prescribing Information and Medication Guide with a revised dosing regimen in patients who have achieved and maintained a complete response or better for a minimum of 6 months, the dosing frequency may be decreased to 1.5 mg/kg every two weeks until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity.

description.text: Converted teclistamab monotherapy to traditional approval and added new indication in combination with daratumumab hyaluronidase-fihj for relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma after at least one prior line of therapy

citations.quote: • Conversion from accelerated approval to traditional approval for teclistamab as monotherapy, in adult patients with relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma who have received at least four prior lines of therapy, including a proteasome inhibitor, an immunomodulatory agent and an anti-CD38 monoclonal antibody.• New indication of teclistamab in combination with daratumumab hyaluronidase-fihj for the treatment of adult patients with relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma who have received at least one prior line of therapy, including a proteasome inhibitor and an immunomodulatory agent.• Modifications to the approved Tecvayli and Talvey risk evaluation and mitigation strategy (REMS) to align with the updated U.S. Prescribing Information.

surrogate_endpoint.text: Overall response rate (ORR) assessed by IRC, observed in MajesTEC-1 (61.8%).

citations.quote: The primary evidence of effectiveness is the overall response rate (ORR) observed in MajesTEC-1 (see Section 8.1.2 – Study Results).
The ORR in the efficacy population was 61.8% (95% CI: 52.1, 70.9).

confirmatory_requirement.text: PMR 4334-1: a randomized clinical trial in patients with RRMM comparing a teclistamab-based regimen to standard therapy (primary endpoint PFS) to verify clinical benefit.
